# Display scaling (`display.scaling`)

**Kind:** action · **Category:** Display · **Runs as:** the signed-in user · **Revertible:** yes

Changes the scale (text, apps and other items size) of a display.

## Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `percent` | whole number (100–500) | yes |  | Scale in percent: 100, 125, 150, 175, 200, 225, 250, 300, 350, 400, 450 or 500. |
| `monitor` | text | no | `primary` | Which display: all, primary, a monitor number (2) or a device name such as \\.\DISPLAY2. Supports [placeholders](../placeholders.md). |
| `continue_on_error` | true / false | no | `false` | Keep running the next actions even if this one fails. |

## Example

```yaml
actions:
  - type: display.scaling
    percent: 150
```

## In profiles

When this action is part of a [profile](../../guide/profiles.md), the current value is saved before it runs and
restored when the profile is reverted. Two actions of this type change the same setting when their `monitor` is the same.

## Notes

Each display only allows the steps up to its maximum (shown in Settings > Display > Scale). This setting has no official programming interface; AutoSettings changes it the way Windows stores it internally. It works on current Windows 10 and 11 builds but may stop working after a Windows update. If it fails, the error says so; use `settings.open` to open the Settings page instead.
